experiment_template.research_question: Does the repaired H45 no-effect fallback combine with H49 effect closure to transfer beyond exposed Round 30 data?
stop_conditions: Dispatch each of eight fresh identities at most once.
No task, prompt, source, policy, cap, scorer, threshold, or token ceiling changes after freeze.
Pass advances only to a separately frozen larger fresh development replication.
Retain missing and failed outcomes as zero; do not replace tasks or rerun for luck.

records.falsifier: Any fixed canary criterion fails, any selected evidence is not receipt-bound pinned-base evidence produced by the declared branch, usage is unknown, or closure adds a model call or token.
records.mechanism: When actual effect hunks exist, retain the unchanged six-item pinned-base overlap closure. Otherwise select the widest delivered pinned-base observation from each of the four most frequently observed paths, breaking path ties by recency and width, and union those IDs with the model selection.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash fresh eight-identity ContextBench development canary at 8K and the 96K primary token tier.
records.statement: Hybrid zero-token terminal closure improves scheduled macro Span-F1 by at least 0.05 on the fresh GLM-5.3-flash 8K canary without degrading coverage, precision, file metrics, or validity.

records.falsifier: H50 meets every fixed canary criterion and the no-effect subgroup contributes positive Span-F1 without file or validity degradation.
records.mechanism: Retain H49 six-item effect closure and suppress closure when no effect hunk exists.

records.statement: Only effect-linked closure is reliable; repeated attention without an effect adds noisy context on fresh tasks.

selection.reason: Round 30 exact reconstruction falsified cap, crop, minimality, and reranking repairs. The four-path no-effect mechanism predates Round 30 in round27b-feature-analysis; H50 repairs pinned-base admission and unions it with the supported effect closure.
